reading.thesis: An eminence-discounted Dragon deck whose engine is the ARRIVAL, not the attack: Miirym copies each nontoken Dragon that arrives, and Terror of the Peaks, Dragon Tempest and Scourge of Valkas price every arrival in damage — a cascade the passing stacks resolve from an assembled board, while the turn that puts two discounted Dragons down to build it is the model's claim, not a verified line. V6 bought a response suite four of whose six additions are castable at instant speed as printed, and two of those four are flash Dragons whose own entry is an arrival; Whirlwing Stormbrood's flash grant and Sneak Attack's unrestricted activation are the main doors for any other Dragon off your own turn — Chaos Warp on your own permanent and Transcendent Dragon's free cast of a countered Dragon spell (CR 608.2g) are narrower ones — and none of it is verified.

lines.name: conversion → output
lines.note: Fifteen Faerie Dragon tokens enter as one event, so Dragon Tempest triggers fifteen times and every trigger sees X = 17 (2 pre-existing Dragons + 15 tokens); 255 damage is available at a single target and the 30-life seat dies to the second. The tokens ARE what Tempest counts and what it triggers on, so the arrow is a feed and not a coincidence. This is the deck's one fully-contained Commander Spellbook line (bracket 3, 'Near-infinite damage', infinite: false), and the record stays a CANDIDATE: 001 fixes the d20 at 15 'for determinism' and starts post-combat-damage, so it verifies the line's resolution on a roll of 15 once Ancient Gold Dragon has already connected — not the connection, which needs an unblocked attack, and not the roll, which averages 10.5.

lines.name: conversion → output
lines.note: Panharmonicon doubles Miirym, so one Lathliss cast becomes two nonlegendary 6/6 copies, and those entries pay Terror 36 across six instances of 6 — of which 24 is attributable to Miirym's two copies, the other 12 being the wave-1 triggers on Lathliss's own entry, which Miirym did not cause. One-directional: Miirym makes the bodies whose entry Terror prices.

lines.name: conversion → output
lines.note: THE UN-DOUBLED FLOOR. Stack 007 step 5 rules that ORIGINAL Lathliss requires a NONTOKEN Dragon, so she makes no 5/5 on this board; the one body is Token A, created by Miirym's single trigger (step 4). Of 007's 20, Terror of the Peaks takes 12 (6+6) and Dragon Tempest 8 (4+4). Split by the entry that caused each trigger, Lathliss's own entry and Token A's are 10 apiece, and of each 10 Terror takes 6 and Dragon Tempest 4 — Terror is in neither via. Dragon Tempest damage that Miirym's body accounts for is FIVE: the 4 of Token A's own Tempest trigger (step 6), plus 1 on the wave-1 Tempest trigger, which counts 4 Dragons instead of 3 only because Token A is on the battlefield when it resolves (step 3's ordering; step 7: 'had the wave-1 Tempest trigger resolved before Miirym's, X would have been 3 and the total 19'). So this pair carries 5 of the 20. The arrow is the Panharmonicon-free version of lines[1] on the identical board, and 007 rules the 20 does not kill the 32-life seat that 002's 64 does.

lines.name: ignition → conversion
lines.note: A CLAIM, and the null is load-bearing. Stack 007 step 8 rules the rules half — eminence is active from the command zone and Lathliss's locked-in cost is {3}{R}{R} — but 007's own scenario declares the full {4}{R}{R} paid 'so the cascade, not the discount, is what is being measured', and the scenario names no Ur-Dragon on any board. So the discount is verified as a rule and unverified as this deck's route into the cascade. What it would buy: a turn where Lathliss and a four-drop Dragon both land, which is what every trigger count downstream assumes.

lines.name: conversion → fuel
lines.note: The one arrow that runs from the engine back into its own fuel, and it is unverified. Ganax reads 'Whenever Ganax or another Dragon you control enters, create a Treasure token' with no nontoken clause, so Miirym's token copies should each pay a Treasure — which would make the cascade fund its own next cast. 001 and 002 both had to settle the token-versus-nontoken question for Miirym and Lathliss, and neither board contained Ganax.

open_questions.question: With Whirlwing Stormbrood // Dynamic Soar on the battlefield, can the deck cast Lathliss, Dragon Queen on an opponent's end step and have the full Miirym / Terror of the Peaks / Dragon Tempest cascade resolve at instant speed — do all the entry triggers behave identically outside your own main phase, and does the Omen half (Dynamic Soar, {2}{G}) matter to the line at all?
open_questions.why_it_matters: This is the single claim V6 was built on: four of six additions are castable at instant speed as printed, and Whirlwing is the card that lets a NON-flash Dragon spell be cast off your own turn, so the pilot stops choosing between developing and holding up a response. It is the `protection -> conversion` arrow in this model, it carries verified_by: null, and no passing stack touches it. If it holds, the protection stage stops being a tax on the pivot turn; if it does not, V6 added responses the deck still cannot afford to hold.

open_questions.question: Repair stack 008 and re-run the checker. Its checker block carries 33 findings, 26 supported and SEVEN not: step 4's 608.2k unsupported (the trigger condition names the Courser, not the commander the effect introduces); step 9's 608.2k misquoted (a zone change is not a changed characteristic); step 10's 508.3a unsupported; and four MISSING STEPS — 702.9b (flying never established, though final_state rules on blocks), 508.1b (attackers never assigned to players, though final_state prints a 19-power total), 603.10 (what actually settles step 10's Atarka answer) and 508.1f (the attackers are tapped).
open_questions.why_it_matters: WITHDRAWN: the previous version said 008 fails on ONE citation and called the work 'a citation repair, not a new scenario'. Both were false — seven findings stand, and four of them require WRITING steps. What the stack would settle is unchanged: three legal attackers (Ganax, Courser, The Ur-Dragon), three cards drawn, one permanent from hand, commander tax unchanged because putting is not casting. Until it passes it appears in no verified_by here and the conversion stage marks its tax answer as unproven. The stake: the commander is cast by turn six in 0.329 of runs, mean cast turn 6.919, and never by turn ten in 2,238 of 10,000, so Courser may be this deck's real commander route.

open_questions.question: Do Twinflame Tyrant and Solphim, Mayhem Dominus both apply to the same damage event — a Dragon Tempest or Terror of the Peaks trigger aimed at an opponent — for four times the printed damage, and if so who chooses the order the two replacement effects apply in (CR 616.1)? Resolve on a board with one doubler, then both, and state the multiplier exactly.
open_questions.why_it_matters: Carried forward unanswered from the v1.0.2 model and still the largest unmeasured quantity here. Neither card appears in a passing stack, in a fully-contained combo line, or in a goldfish leg that treats it as a multiplier. If both apply, stack 002's board reads 256 rather than 64 and 007's ceiling — that 64 cannot kill both seats, since 64 < 72 — stops being a ceiling.

What do that target and interaction_castable_by_turn read then, against the CURRENT 0.823 assembled / 0.716 by turn six and 0.306 / 0.395 / 0.481?
open_questions.why_it_matters: WITHDRAWN AND RESCOPED. Round 1 called this 'the single edit without which nothing in the record measures what changed today', described a six-card leg and quoted 0.665 / 0.557. All three were wrong at the time of writing: goldfish_targets.json declares NINE cards on that leg, labelled 'v1.3.0 added three: Asceticism, Mithril Coat, Stubborn Denial', and deck-audit now prints 0.823 / 0.716 over that size-9 component (0.811 / 0.713 before the 2026-10-28 re-measure). Three of the four cards round 1 proposed adding were already there and the re-run it asked for had already happened. What survives is one card: Transcendent Dragon is in goldfish_metrics meta.interaction_suite_counted but not in the declared leg, and it is a flash counterspell that is also a body the conversion tier triggers on. Whirlwing Stormbrood is the other undeclared response, but it belongs in the SECOND target proposed below rather than this one, because it protects nothing itself.

open_questions.question: Can this deck actually hold {4}{U}{U} up for Transcendent Dragon on the turn it wants to pivot? Blue is 20 total sources against a 22 yardstick with on-curve 0.881, but the card is six mana and the cascade turn is the same turn.
open_questions.why_it_matters: Transcendent Dragon is the most expensive response in the deck and, with Whirlwing Stormbrood, one of two flash Dragons that are also bodies the engine triggers on, so its value is entirely a question of whether the mana exists twice. interaction_castable_by_turn is 0.481 at turn six and the model's own note calls that a FLOOR because it spends rather than holds — which means the figure that would answer this does not exist yet in either direction.

open_questions.question: Activate Sneak Attack on an opponent's end step, putting Lathliss, Dragon Queen onto the battlefield beside Miirym, Terror of the Peaks and Dragon Tempest. Does the cascade resolve exactly as stack 007's does on your own turn; when is Lathliss sacrificed, given that 'the beginning of the next end step' has already passed in the end step it arrived in; and do Miirym's token copies, which Sneak Attack did not put onto the battlefield, stay?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The thesis and lines[7] name Sneak Attack as the second door to an arrival off your own turn, resting on its ability carrying no timing restriction (CR 117.1b). No stack has resolved it at instant speed, and if the answer to the sacrifice question is 'at your own end step', the cheated Lathliss survives a full turn — which would make Sneak Attack a deploy rather than a one-turn loan.

open_questions.question: ANSWERED IN PART BY STACK 009 (one creature: ordered sacrifice-first, Gadrak makes one Treasure, priority before cleanup). What remains: with two creatures put in by Sneak Attack this turn, do both delayed sacrifices go on above Gadrak's trigger so it counts two and makes two Treasures, and on a board with an instant in hand does the end-step window actually cast it?
open_questions.why_it_matters: lines[8] stands on 009's single activation. The model reads Sneak Attack's lack of an activation limit as one Treasure refunded per creature, which is the repeatability claim 009 does not make; and the off-turn response that refund is meant to pay for is a card the 009 board did not hold. absent_stages[0] keeps the no-fodder verdict either way, because the Treasure is a rebate on the Dragon Sneak Attack already sacrifices.

findings.claim: conversion -> fuel via Sneak Attack and Gadrak, carries mana: 'Sneak Attack's sacrifice is what Gadrak pays for'
findings.note: Stack 009 shows the flow itself, not just a board that names both cards. Its checker verdict is pass with no non-supported finding. What 009 resolves, step by step: Gadrak has been on the battlefield since an earlier turn. Glorybringer, a nontoken card Dragon that is in the decklist, was put in by Sneak Attack in precombat main. No creature has died earlier this turn. Steps 1-2: both end-step triggers are yours and you order them (603.3b) with the sacrifice on top. Step 4: Glorybringer is sacrificed and is the only death this turn. Step 6: Gadrak counts on resolution, finds 1 and creates one Treasure, and the step states that the reverse order makes 0. Step 7: you get priority again in the end step with the Treasure untapped. final_state lists the Treasure on the battlefield and Glorybringer in the graveyard. So the death that Sneak Attack (conversion stage) causes is what Gadrak (fuel stage) turns into a Treasure. The arrow's direction, its via cards and 'carries mana' all match the resolution, and the rule numbers the note cites (603.3b, 608.2h, 117.3b, 500.2) are the ones 009's summary cites. The note's list of what 009 does not prove is accurate: the hand is empty, there is one activation, and Gadrak is already out and survives. It puts the repeatability claim on the model's side, not the stack's. This is unlike the two radagast failures: the 009 board makes the Treasure, it does not leave it unmade.

findings.claim: 'that every activation refunds a Treasure is this model's reading of an unlimited ability, not the stack's finding'
findings.note: This is correctly kept out of the solid arrow. Sneak Attack's oracle text has no activation limit, and Gadrak counts 'each nontoken creature that died this turn', so the reading is plausible. It is unproven and labelled unproven, and open_questions[6] carries it forward as a residual.

findings.claim: 'ANSWERED IN PART BY STACK 009' with residual: two Sneak Attack creatures -> two Treasures, and an actual instant cast in the window
findings.note: The part marked answered matches 009's three answers, (a), (b) and (c). The two residuals are exactly what 009's scenario leaves out: its hand is empty, and only one creature is on it. Both are well formed for resolve-stack. why_it_matters no longer makes any claim beyond the stack. 'A rebate on the Dragon Sneak Attack already sacrifices' fits 009, where the sacrificed creature is Glorybringer, a Dragon.

findings.claim: Crux's non-Dragon mode kills 'the five dorks, Dragonlord's Servant, Dragonspeaker Shaman, Solphim'; Desolation 'the same minus Solphim (toughness 4), and minus Faeburrow Elder when you control four or more colours'
findings.note: ROUND-4 FINDING RESOLVED. cards.json has exactly eight non-Dragon creatures: Birds of Paradise 0/1, Bloom Tender 1/1, Delighted Halfling 1/2, Faeburrow Elder 0/0 (W/G), Ignoble Hierarch 0/1, Dragonlord's Servant 1/3, Dragonspeaker Shaman 2/2, and Solphim (Phyrexian Horror, 5/4). Crux's list is all eight. Desolation's 3 damage kills each one with toughness 3 or less. Solphim survives at toughness 4. Faeburrow gets +1/+1 per colour among your permanents and counts its own W and G, so its toughness equals your colour count: it dies at three colours or fewer and survives at four or more, which is exactly what the text says. 'Crux a payoff too' is correct because Solphim is a damage doubler. Gadrak and Atsushi are both Dragons, and Crux's Dragon mode kills both: correct. The dies|died sweep (Atsushi and Gadrak only), the eleven 'sacrific' cards, 'nothing in the 99 returns it', and the list of any-target damage triggers all still match cards.json, as re-verified in round 4. Trimming the field to 2,011 characters cut the loose 'a 4-damage trigger' wording, which resolves that note too.

unmatched_v1_lines.note: Panharmonicon doubles every trigger in the cascade, because each is caused by a creature entering — Tempest's six instances read 4,4,5,5,5,5 for 28. It multiplies the payoff and not only the bodies, and stack 007 measures the counterfactual on the same board: without it the whole cascade deals 20.

The deck's only checker-passed arrow that reaches a finisher. {R} puts Drakuseth in with haste, the attack trigger fires the same turn for 4+3+3, it connects for 7, and all 17 stands after the mandatory end-step sacrifice. The same stack refutes this arrow ever pointing at the commander: 903.6, the command zone is not the hand.

V6's thesis as a single arrow, and nothing verifies it. Whirlwing reads 'You may cast sorcery spells and Dragon spells as though they had flash', so with it on the battlefield Lathliss can be cast on an opponent's end step with mana held up through the turn cycle for Stubborn Denial and Mithril Coat. It is not the only door off your own turn: Transcendent Dragon and Whirlwing are themselves flash Dragons whose entry is an arrival, and Sneak Attack's '{R}: You may put a creature card from your hand onto the battlefield' carries no 'activate only as a sorcery' clause (CR 117.1b: an activated ability may be activated any time its controller has priority). If any of it holds, the deck stops choosing between developing and responding — the choice prescription 0241fb6a70f1 says it kept losing.

Sneak Attack's sacrifice is what Gadrak pays for. Both trigger at the beginning of your end step; you order them (603.3b) so the sacrifice resolves first, Gadrak counts 'each nontoken creature that died this turn' on resolution (608.2h) and makes one Treasure, and you get priority again before cleanup (117.3b, 500.2). Reversed, it makes zero. What 009 does NOT prove: its hand is empty, so it shows the Treasure CAN pay for an instant in that window, not that the deck has one to cast then; and it is ONE activation on one board, so that every activation refunds a Treasure is this model's reading of an unlimited ability, not the stack's finding. Gadrak must already be on the battlefield and survive to the end step.

v1_stages.label: THE FIVE-COLOUR TOLL, PAID TWICE
v1_stages.what_it_does:
A nine-mana commander and a curve of six-drops in five colours, and the deck pays that toll twice: 32 land entries / 35 copies, then 23 ramp copies against strategy:deckbuilding.ratios' 10-12, which deck-audit calls OVER. A build choice — eminence discounts GENERIC mana — but mana-base still reads UNDER at 35 against 36-38, and colour-sources UNDER by nine on black: 21 sources with rocks and dorks against a yardstick of 30, on-curve 0.729 where every other colour is 0.822 or better.

'Ramp or fixing drawn' assembles in 0.906 of 10,000 runs at mean turn 2.268; mean available mana is 5.944 at turn five. Land drops fray, 0.756 at turn four and 0.624 at turn five, and that figure cannot be about taplands: the goldfish assumes LANDS ENTER UNTAPPED, ALWAYS, so it measures whether a land is in hand, not how it enters. On tapped lands deck-audit's taplands axis reads 1 against a ceiling of 8, verdict AT — Path of Ancestry — and mana_analysis's 12 is a superset. The other eleven are CONDITIONAL, and only six are a choice: the six shocks pay 2 life. Dragonskull Summit wants a Swamp or Mountain, Canopy Vista, Cinder Glade and Smoldering Marsh two basics, and Turbulent Springs enters untapped only if OPPONENTS control eight or more lands.

Five sources are RESTRICTED per deck-facts — Cavern of Souls, Delighted Halfling, Desolation of Smaug, Maelstrom of the Spirit Dragon, Unclaimed Territory pay for spells only. Desolation sits here, not output: its four Dragon-only mana is why it is in the 99, and deck-audit prices it as the one single point of failure, a one-card component at 0.167 assembled.

Pips explain the fetches and V6's Forest-to-Mountain: 31 cards want {R} for 48 pips, against 17 and 19 green.

v1_stages.label: THE PRICE CUT, LIVE FROM TURN ONE
v1_stages.what_it_does:
The first thing that has to happen is a Dragon costing less than it says. Eminence is the only part of this engine an opponent cannot answer: The Ur-Dragon discounts other Dragon spells {1} FROM THE COMMAND ZONE, live on turn one with nothing on the battlefield to remove. Stack 007 step 8 rules it, citing 601.2f, and prices Lathliss at {3}{R}{R} rather than her printed {4}{R}{R} — 'a cost reduction is not optional and the printed {4}{R}{R} is not payable as written'. The four cards here stack on top of it: Dragonlord's Servant ({1} less) and Dragonspeaker Shaman ({2} less) are Dragon-specific; Urza's Incubator ({2}) and Herald's Horn ({1}) name a creature type as they enter.

What this stage buys is not one cheap Dragon, it is TWO IN ONE TURN, which is the assumption every trigger downstream is priced against — a six-drop at {3}{R}{R} plus a four-drop at three is eight mana instead of ten.

Measured: 'Cost reducer drawn' assembles in 0.523 of 10,000 runs, 0.423 by turn six, mean turn 3.253 — 0.666 and 0.55 with tutors counted. 'Reducer + ramp assembled (the turn-5-Ur-Dragon hand)' is 0.467 / 0.339. So roughly half the deck's games are played at eminence's {1} alone.

Note what this stage does NOT buy. The commander itself is on the battlefield by turn six in 0.329 of runs, mean cast turn 6.919, median 7, and is never cast by turn ten in 2,238 of 10,000. Eminence is doing this deck's ignition from a zone the game will not let anyone touch; the body is a bonus. That is also why no card here is a single point of failure — the one piece that must be live cannot be removed, and the other four are redundant with each other.

v1_stages.label: TREASURE, TWO DRAGONSTORMS THAT COME BACK, AND THE DRAW THE GOLDFISH DOES NOT MODEL
v1_stages.what_it_does:
Once a Dragon has landed the deck needs two things it is short of: mana for the SECOND Dragon the same turn, and cards.

Six Treasure sources cover the first — Atsushi, Gadrak, Ganax, Goldspan Dragon, Old Gnawbone and Smaug the Magnificent. 'A Treasure source drawn' assembles in 0.672 of runs, 0.562 by turn six. Read the hoard as a FLOOR: goldfish meta.treasure_sources_not_modelled names Atsushi, Gadrak and Ganax as sources it cannot see, so 0.428 Treasures at turn six and 1.853 at turn ten are what the other three produce. Stack 009 proves one Gadrak route: a Sneak Attack creature sacrificed at your end step pays a Treasure (lines[8]). Treasure is a stockpile, not a rock: it buys one expensive turn and does not raise mean available mana, so it sits here and not in mana.

Cards are the thinner half. deck-audit reads card-advantage UNDER at 4 copies against a floor of 10, and its own note says the count misses Dragon's Hoard and Sunbaked Canyon, which do the job in words no taxonomy pattern matches. What actually refills: Garruk's Uprising and Temur Ascendancy each draw when a creature with power 4 or greater enters — the same event the output stage is built on, so the engine pays for its own next card — Dragon's Hoard banks a gold counter per Dragon entering and cashes them one at a time, and both Dragonstorms RETURN TO HAND when a Dragon enters — Roiling draws two and discards one, Breaching is impulse access, not a draw.

Two tutors sit here because they find the missing piece rather than ramp: Enlightened Tutor (Panharmonicon, Sneak Attack, Dragon Tempest) and Sarkhan's Triumph (any Dragon), both at instant speed. The goldfish models a cast tutor as filling one missing any_of group, which is the gap between every unassisted rate in this model and its assisted twin.

v1_stages.label: ONE ARRIVAL BECOMES SEVERAL, AND EVERY POINT BECOMES TWO
v1_stages.what_it_does:
The engine proper, in two tiers that multiply different things.

MORE ARRIVALS. Miirym copies every other nontoken Dragon that enters; Lathliss makes a 5/5 for each (oracle text — it fires on no passing board); Ancient Gold Dragon rolls a d20 on combat damage and makes that many 1/1 flying Faerie Dragons; Panharmonicon fires a permanent's triggered ability an additional time when an ARTIFACT OR CREATURE entering caused it — not an enchantment or a land. Sneak Attack puts a CREATURE CARD from hand onto the battlefield for {R} with haste — the scope stack 005 turns on — and Hellkite Courser's entry puts the commander from the command zone with haste until the next end step. That the commander tax is untouched is stack 008's answer, and 008 has not passed. Token-versus-nontoken is the brake 001 and 002 both had to settle: token copies do not re-trigger Miirym or Lathliss, so the cascade terminates.

MORE DAMAGE PER POINT. Twinflame Tyrant doubles all damage a source you control deals to an opponent or their permanents, Solphim doubles NONCOMBAT damage only, Thrakkus doubles each Dragon's power when it attacks, and Atarka grants an attacking Dragon double strike. Read against the output stage, Twinflame and Solphim both apply to Terror of the Peaks and Dragon Tempest damage aimed at an opponent — and NONE of the four is verified: no fully-contained combo record, no passing stack.

single_point_of_failure is null by judgement. Stack 007 is brutal about ONE board — cutting Panharmonicon takes 002 from 64 damage in twelve instances to 20 in four, 'its LETHALITY, not just its margin', a 68.75% loss — but deck-audit names only Desolation of Smaug, Panharmonicon sits in no goldfish component, and the cascade runs without it.

v1_stages.label: WHAT AN ARRIVAL IS WORTH
v1_stages.what_it_does:
What the deck points at a table, and it is priced per ARRIVAL rather than per attack. Terror of the Peaks deals the entering creature's power to any target; Dragon Tempest and Scourge of Valkas deal X where X counts your Dragons and X is recomputed at each trigger's resolution.

Stack 002 measures one Lathliss cast into a four-permanent board at 64 damage in twelve separately-targeted instances — 36 from Terror across six triggers, 28 from Tempest at X = 4,4,5,5,5,5 under optimal ordering — which kills a 32-life seat. Stack 007 step 9 then settles the harder question: every one of those twelve instances reads 'any target', a player is a legal choice for all of them, and aimed at one seat the running total reaches 42 by the eighth instance, so that board CAN kill a player at 40. Stack 001 is the same machine larger: fifteen tokens enter as one event, every Tempest trigger sees X = 17, and 255 damage is available.

Firespitter Whelp is the odd member of the payoff tier and the only one of its four that needs no body to enter: 1 to each opponent whenever you cast a noncreature OR Dragon spell.

The rest is interaction, which deck-audit reads as 11 copies against a floor of 8 but only FOUR classes answered against a floor of five, with graveyard detected as unanswered. Enumerated: Swords to Plowshares and Generous Gift are unconditional single-target answers, Chaos Warp reaches any permanent at instant speed, Crux of Fate is the UNCONDITIONAL sweeper and one of two on deck-audit's sweepers axis, Glorybringer exerts for 4 to a non-Dragon creature, and Steel Hellkite — new in V6 — destroys every nonland permanent of a chosen mana value controlled by a player it dealt combat damage to, once each turn.

v1_stages.label: THE ANSWER TO 'I NOW HAVE ZERO RESPONSES'
v1_stages.what_it_does:
Prescription 0241fb6a70f1, after five games at 1W 4L: 'speed without protection or politics makes me the obvious kill target before I can close.' Five of V6's six spell additions land here (the sixth, Steel Hellkite, is in output), and FOUR of the six are castable at instant speed as printed — Stubborn Denial is an instant; Mithril Coat, Transcendent Dragon and Whirlwing Stormbrood have flash; Asceticism and Steel Hellkite do not. What V6 bought is not more protection, it is protection that can be held up.

Asceticism is the only always-on PROTECTION in the 99 covering more than one creature (Greaves and Coat cover one each): board hexproof, plus regeneration for {1}{G}. Mithril Coat has flash, is itself indestructible and attaches free to a legendary creature as it enters — with 12 legendary creatures here, a three-mana flash artifact that blanks a removal spell. Stubborn Denial is {U} and hard-counters any noncreature spell while you control a 4-power creature — nearly every Dragon here. Transcendent Dragon counters a spell, exiles it and lets you cast it free: a response that is also a body every conversion trigger fires on. Whirlwing Stormbrood protects nothing itself: while it is on the battlefield sorceries and Dragon spells have flash, so mana held for a response can still deploy. UNVERIFIED — no passing stack touches it.

The five older pieces cost held mana all game, and two read 'if you control a commander' — the commander is on the battlefield by turn six in 0.329 of runs, so Flawless Maneuver and Deflecting Swat usually are not free. interaction_castable_by_turn reads 0.306 / 0.395 / 0.481 on turns four to six, and the model's own note calls that a FLOOR. Thunderbreak Regent only PRICES removal, 3 damage to its caster; of the twelve it stops nothing.

v1_stages.label: PROVEN ON A BOARD, THIN AS A ROUTE
v1_stages.what_it_does:
Two cards, and the thinness is the finding rather than a hole in the model: this deck does not close with a finisher, it closes with the cascade, and every card that does that work is already earning its slot in conversion or output. What is left is the two whose only job is to end the game. Drakuseth, Maw of Flames deals 4 + 3 + 3 to any targets whenever it ATTACKS — an attack trigger, not a cast trigger, so it fires the turn Sneak Attack cheats it in and all 17 damage stands after the mandatory end-step sacrifice (stack 005). Scourge of the Throne untaps all attacking creatures and adds a combat phase the first time it attacks the player with the most life, which is the one card here that doubles an already-lethal board rather than building one.

What is checker-passed: stack 001's board kills BOTH opponents; stack 002's kills the 32-life seat with 64 damage and, per 007 step 9, can reach 42 at a single seat and so kill a player at 40; stack 005 lands 17 for {R} off Sneak Attack, four lands and a Drakuseth in hand. What is NOT checker-passed is any line that gets from an ordinary turn six to one of those boards — every stack starts from a board already assembled.

Against the goldfish's one 40-life opponent that never blocks, median kill turn is 7, mean 7.376, with 0.238 by turn six, 0.542 by turn seven and 0.052 of runs never killing by turn ten; mean board power is 14.706 at turn six and 19.642 at turn seven. Read that as an unopposed clock on ONE seat, not a win rate — and read it against the prescription that named being killed first as the problem, because a deck this fast in a goldfish is a deck a table sees coming.

v1_map_disagreements.component: THE CASCADE ITSELF — stack 002's five cards at three addresses
v1_map_disagreements.why: Stack 002 is the deck's measured engine: Lathliss cast into Miirym, Terror of the Peaks, Dragon Tempest and Panharmonicon, 64 damage. The map puts Miirym, Lathliss and Terror in THE AIR FORCE (and in three different neighbourhoods of it), Dragon Tempest in THE SETUP's WHEN DRAGONS LAND, and Panharmonicon in THE GEAR. The cartographer's note says as much. The reason is the space: CardBERT reads typed fields, so a creature, an enchantment and an artifact with the same 'enters' trigger land apart. The engine is a relation between card types, and the map is a grouping by card type, so the one thing the deck does is the one thing the constellation cannot draw.

v1_map_disagreements.component: THE AIR FORCE read as an engine part
v1_map_disagreements.why: 27 cards, 28% of the 97 entries, holding members of SIX of my seven stages: conversion 8, fuel 6, output 5, ignition 3, protection 3, wincon 2. It is not a stage, and its gloss — 'every arrival here discounts the next under eminence' — is false of FOUR members: Dragonlord's Servant (Goblin Shaman), Dragonspeaker Shaman (Human Barbarian Shaman) and Solphim, Mayhem Dominus (Phyrexian Horror) are not Dragons, and eminence discounts only 'OTHER Dragon spells', so it never discounts The Ur-Dragon, the city's fourth exception. (Read the other way — the arriving card doing the discounting — the gloss is true of only the commander and the two reducers.) What the city collects is creatures; that a deck of Dragons is mostly creatures makes it look like a reading.

v1_map_disagreements.component: V6'S RESPONSE SUITE — six additions, four addresses
v1_map_disagreements.why: The six V6 spell additions answer one prescription and the map files them by card type: Asceticism in THE SETUP (an enchantment), Mithril Coat in THE GEAR (an equipment), Stubborn Denial in THE INSURANCE (an instant), Transcendent Dragon, Whirlwing Stormbrood and Steel Hellkite in THE AIR FORCE (Dragons). THE INSURANCE's gloss, 'held up, not cast', describes the job the four instant-speed additions were bought for, yet only Stubborn Denial is in it — the three flash permanents are elsewhere — while the city holds Crux of Fate, a sorcery that can be held up only under Whirlwing. Four of the six are castable at instant speed as printed (Stubborn Denial, plus flash on Mithril Coat, Transcendent Dragon and Whirlwing), and Steel Hellkite, a Dragon, becomes so while Whirlwing is on the battlefield; only Asceticism is a plain sorcery-speed permanent. That sentence is in no card's text.

v1_map_disagreements.component: THE DAMAGE MULTIPLIERS — one city, three neighbourhoods, and a declaration that disagrees with both
v1_map_disagreements.why: All four multipliers are creatures and so all four sit in THE AIR FORCE, which looks like agreement and is not: Twinflame Tyrant is in hood-0 THE ENABLERS, Atarka and Thrakkus in hood-1, Solphim in hood-2. The declaration splits them a third way: goldfish_targets' COMBAT KILL multiplier leg names only Atarka and Thrakkus and counts Twinflame Tyrant AND Solphim as 'a Dragon to attack with' — and Solphim is not a Dragon, and doubles only noncombat damage.

v1_map_disagreements.component: THE COST REDUCERS — split on card type
v1_map_disagreements.why: engine-facts' scatter table puts the four-card 'Cost reducer drawn' component across two cities at 2 / 2: Dragonlord's Servant and Dragonspeaker Shaman in THE AIR FORCE, Herald's Horn and Urza's Incubator in THE GEAR. Every one of them reads 'cost {N} less'; what the map hears is creature versus artifact.

v1_map_disagreements.component: 'Ramp or fixing drawn' — the widest scatter in the brief
v1_map_disagreements.why: engine-facts' scatter table puts this 12-card component across three cities at 5 / 4 / 3 and marks it incoherent, and it is the component the deck depends on most (0.906 assembled). Dorks are creatures, rocks and Dragon's Hoard are artifacts, and Farseek, Nature's Lore and Skyshroud Claim say 'search your library', which files three land-ramp sorceries beside Enlightened Tutor. All twelve answer one question — can I pay for a six-drop on turn four — and the map sorts them by what they are rather than by that.
